findings.reason: the node either measures against a non-finite reference and reports a false failure, or silently substitutes a different state, and the plan should name the states where the present route's read is valid (the limited converged and diverted trial states) instead.
findings.text: §3's done-when (1) compares "one fast step's update" with "the present route's Newton update" at the limited and diverted 550-cell trial states, but `read-derivative-prototype` records `read valid: no` for the production read at the limited trial state (every row, including the exact analytic-derivative oracle), and `solve-wall-breakdown` (:113) makes `nova.equilibrium.topology.read` the present step's read stage while `support_read.read` invalidates the whole read on any unconverged point and books non-finite moments from an invalid read (`support_read.py:113`, `support_read.book` :121–127) — so at the limited trial state the present route has no established finite Newton update to compare against, and the clause is not measurable there as written

findings.reason: a node cannot tell whether clause (1) is satisfied by an accurate position from an invalid read or must first repair the qualification gate, and it has no plan-sanctioned route to the X-point the clause demands.
findings.text: §2's done-when (1) requires the axis within 5e-4 of the minor radius at the limited trial and diverted converged states and an X-point at the diverted trial and converged states, but `read-derivative-prototype` records `read valid: no` for every read at the limited trial state and states "No row admits an X-point, including every oracle row, so no X-point error is reported"; §2 changes the derivative source and the rebuild strategy only and says nothing about the validity/qualification gate (`support_read.read` returns `valid = jnp.all(solved.valid) & reading.valid & reading.qualified`, :113) or about the saddle branch — so the clause does not state whether a read that reports itself invalid may satisfy it, and its X-point requirement has no stated mechanism to make an X-point admitted

findings.reason: the 0.2 ms steady-state bound rests on tracking removing the whole stage, and if the ~29 ms of per-call device data movement is not produced by the rebuild the section needs a stated change to the per-call operand transfer before its bound is reachable.
findings.text: §2 attributes the present read's whole 107.8 ms to "rebuilding the connected-domain decision and contour tree" ("the tree's loop body alone takes 18.4 ms … and its fragment and fusion kernels take the rest"), but the `solve-wall-breakdown` device trace it cites records only 18.394 ms as the `build_contour_tree` while-loop body, a separate 29.4 ms of device memcpy per call (27% of the stage, absent from the plan's accounting), 39.618 ms of unnamed XLA fusion kernels the trace does not place inside the tree, and 17.935 ms of a separate reads' while-loop body — so the cited trace does not show that the rebuild accounts for the stage the mechanism claims to remove

findings.reason: an implementer who converges the inner solve tightly meets both clauses, so the omission costs a sentence rather than a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §3 permits the Jacobian to be "applied either as one dense block or matrix-free inside a Krylov solve", while its done-when (1) and (3) both demand a 1e-6 relative agreement (update against the present route, JVP against central differences), and the inner Krylov tolerance that sets the update's agreement is never stated

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every code anchor in s2 and s3 resolves (`support_read.read` :78, `support_read.read_and_book` :130, `fixed_points.solve` :646, `fixed_points.RowCache` :364 / `maintain_rows` :413, `stencil_nulls._quadratic_fit_matrices` :412, `_fit_selected_cells` :378), and the changed figures now match `read-derivative-prototype` exactly (0.51–0.72 ms per call over all 1,743 nodes; 141–144 ms for the jet-consuming read) and `solve-wall-breakdown` (61,330 launches, 18.4 ms tree loop body).
